title: SharePoint forms: Power Automate trigger "When a form is submitted" and action "Get form metadata"
summary: Hold: the data-policy navigation stops at the policy list rather than the connector classification control. The permissions guidance also omits the System Administrator role required for environment-level policies in environments with Dataverse. The feature description and roadmap targets are supported.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing
claims.claim: The SharePoint connector documents the trigger When a form is submitted and the action Get form metadata.
claims.quote:
### When a form is submitted
Triggers a flow when a form in SharePoint is submitted.
### Get form metadata
Gets info about the form.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy reaches the control deciding connector combinations.
claims.quote: From the list of data policies, select a policy, and then select Edit Policy. ... Select one or more pre-built connectors. ... select the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors, and then select Move to Business from the top menu bar.
claims.fix: Replace the path in front matter, rendered table and checklist with 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > SharePoint > Move to Business'. The cited page documents selecting and editing a policy and classifying SharePoint; stopping at Data policy only reaches the list.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification Confidential -Connectors <connector objects> moves connectors into the Business group.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively). ... -Connectors ... Object[] ... -PolicyName ... The policy name (GUID).

claims.where: controls[0].governs, scope; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing data policies govern which connectors flows can combine with SharePoint in their scoped environments.
claims.quote: By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SharePoint is not blockable in a data policy, so the Block action is unavailable.
claims.quote: For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment Admin or Power Platform admin permissions suffice to create or edit the data policy.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead. ... Environment admins can't edit policies created by the tenant admin.
claims.fix: Replace the permissions sentence in the control note and Governance controls with: 'Tenant-level policies require the Power Platform Administrator role. Environment-level policies require Environment Admin permissions, or the System Administrator role for environments with a Dataverse database. Environment admins cannot edit policies created by the tenant admin.'
